# clickhouse-nyctaxi dataset

Moved verbatim from `CLAUDE.md` to keep that file lean. Read it only when working on this topic.

- **`clickhouse-nyctaxi` dataset**: unlike the two QA-image-backed datasets, this one needs source data the repo can't ship (no pre-seeded ClickHouse QA image exists). `make download-nyctaxi` (or `bash scripts/download-nyctaxi-data.sh [year] [taxi-type]`) is a **manual, one-time** step — NOT run automatically by `make new`/`start`/`nuke` — that downloads a year of yellow-taxi Parquet from NYC TLC's CloudFront URL into gitignored `data/clickhouse-nyctaxi/`. `YEAR` is optional and defaults to `2025` (the most recent fully-published year as of when this was written) — deliberately zero-config since this is meant to be a quick one-time step, not a decision point; pass `YEAR=<yyyy>` only to override. Downloads use `curl --retry 5 --retry-all-errors` — plain `--retry` only covers transport failures (timeouts/5xx), not local write errors (e.g. antivirus scanning a file mid-write, which caused real, reproducible `curl: (23)` failures on Windows during testing even though the destination path/disk were fine) — so `--retry-all-errors` is required for those to actually retry instead of failing the file outright. `compose/datasets/clickhouse-nyctaxi.yml` bind-mounts that fixed host folder (read-write — see the gotcha bullet below for why) into ClickHouse's `user_files_path`, separately from the dataset's normal `external: true` `sample_dwh_data` volume (which holds ClickHouse's own native/MergeTree storage and is wiped by `make nuke` like any other dataset). This split is deliberate: nuking or recreating a `clickhouse-nyctaxi` stack never re-triggers a download, since the bind-mounted source files live outside Docker's volume management entirely. `scripts/seed-sample-dwh.sh`'s ClickHouse branch just creates one convenience view (`nyc_taxi_trips_files`, via `file('nyctaxi/*.parquet', Parquet)`) — it errors clearly if the download script hasn't been run yet rather than silently creating an empty/broken view. `scripts/seed-metabase.sh` skips content-seeding entirely for this dataset (no `orders`/`people`/`products` tables exist here, unlike the other two) — cache policy still gets applied, but no demo collection/cards/dashboard.
- **Two `clickhouse-nyctaxi` container-startup gotchas, both confirmed live via `docker logs`/`docker exec`, not guessed:**
  1. The official `clickhouse/clickhouse-server` entrypoint recursively `chown`s everything under `/var/lib/clickhouse` to the `clickhouse` user before it starts the server, and aborts under `set -e` the instant any `chown` fails. A `:ro` bind mount anywhere under that tree (the taxi-data mount was originally `:ro`) makes every file's `chown` fail, and the container exits 1 before ClickHouse ever boots — `docker logs` on the dead container showed *only* the entrypoint's `chown` errors, nothing from the server itself. The mount must stay read-write; nothing in this dataset's design ever writes into it at runtime (`file()` only reads), so that costs nothing in practice. Don't "fix" this back to `:ro`.
  2. The `healthcheck:` must hit `http://127.0.0.1:8123/ping`, not `http://localhost:8123/ping`. Confirmed live: busybox `wget` inside this image resolves `localhost` to `::1` first, but the container's ClickHouse only listens on IPv4 (its own log shows `Listen [::]:8123 failed` — a Docker Desktop/WSL2 IPv6-in-container quirk) and `wget` doesn't fall back to IPv4 on refusal, so every single healthcheck failed with `Connection refused` even while the server was answering real HTTP requests on the published port the entire time. Same class of gotcha as the `127.0.0.1`-not-`$MB_SITE_URL` note for MCP registration above — `localhost` resolving to `::1` first is a recurring trap in this repo's Windows/Docker Desktop environment, worth the same suspicion anywhere else a healthcheck or same-machine loopback call gets added.
